title: How Small Early Edges Snowball Into Giant Leads (Matthew Effect)
alt_title_1: Robert Merton's 1968 Science Study on Cumulative Advantage
alt_title_2: Why Shipping Imperfectly Today Beats Waiting Two Years
description_hook: In a landmark 1968 Science paper studying Nobel laureates, sociologist Robert K. Merton coined the Matthew Effect: tiny initial edges attract disproportionate recognition, capital, and opportunities that snowball over time.

scenes.headline: How Tiny Head Starts Become Giant Gaps
scenes.stat_label: EQUAL TALENT AT START, UNEQUAL OUTCOME AT YEAR 5
bullets: Two peers begin with almost identical ability
One tiny early win recruits the next ten
scenes.narration: Why do two equally talented builders start a hair apart in January and finish five years later in completely different leagues?
scenes.source: Robert K. Merton, 'The Matthew Effect in Science', Science (1968)

scenes.headline: Robert Merton's 1968 'Science' Discovery
bullets: Early visibility drew better labs, grants, and collaborators
Initial advantage multiplied independent of raw IQ
scenes.narration: In a 1968 Science paper studying Nobel laureates, sociologist Robert K. Merton named this cumulative advantage the Matthew Effect: a slight early lead attracts disproportionate credit, resources, and better opportunities that compound.
scenes.source: Robert K. Merton, Science (1968); Harriet Zuckerman Nobel interviews

scenes.headline: Perfectionism Forfeits the Early Snowball
scenes.left_body: Polishes in private -> zero feedback loops, zero early capital
scenes.right_body: Ships Version 1.0 today -> feedback, search trust & cash compound
scenes.narration: Perfectionists misread this math. Waiting two years until your portfolio or skill feels polished hands every early feedback loop and distribution edge to someone shipping today.

scenes.headline: Optimize for Your Earliest Valid Rep
scenes.stat_label: TIME ON THE CURVE BEATS A POLISHED LATE ENTRY
scenes.stat_subtext: Start $100 index auto-transfers + publish Asset #1 this weekend
scenes.narration: Optimize for earliest valid rep, not flashiest debut: automate your first small index transfer and publish version one while peers are still planning.

scenes.headline: Let Early Wins Recruit Future Leverage
bullets: Every public brick compounds reputation while you sleep
Early capital earns years of extra market doublings
scenes.narration: Get onto the cumulative advantage curve early, and let small wins recruit the next round of leverage.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Robert K. Merton, Science (1968)
